Even if the user wanted to exit, intent execution and withdrawals are paused — but the action framework says "you cannot move funds, only propose an action." The action options: hold, reduce_light, reduce_to_target, exit, relever.

Given the position is effectively insolvent-backed and paused, the appropriate proposed action is "exit" — attempt to withdraw/unwind the whole position now. Even though paused, proposing exit is the right keeper response; if execution is blocked, the corridor limits enforce safety. Alternatively "hold" because nothing can be done? The instructions say staying put during a real incident can leave funds stuck or lost. The keeper proposes; execution may fail due to pause. The best action is exit — attempt to unwind now. Actually, with ALL paused, exit attempts would fail. But the framework asks to propose an action; exit is the correct risk response. Some might argue hold since nothing is executable, but the guidance emphasizes not staying put during real incidents. Exit is the strongest protective action and signals to attempt withdrawal the moment it's possible, or attempt now.

Risk level: critical.

Reasons:
- Ledger vs held divergence: 99.78% of BSC-USDT ledger unbacked (O11, O12) — the balance is an unbacked IOU.
- Full pause of deposits/withdrawals/intents (O13) — funds frozen, exit currently blocked; classic incident response.
- Rapid deterioration over ~7 hours from fully backed to ~0% backed (O06→O12) suggests active drain/exploit of HOT Omni bridge or intents.near reserves.
- Bitget theft (O04) and SKYDAO exploit (O05) are unrelated to this venue — not drivers.
